audit_status.source_base: Greek Gospel text tradition, draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Sabbath grainfields, Sabbath healing, choosing the Twelve, plain sermon blessings/woes, enemy-love, mercy, judging, tree/fruit, and foundation sayings.

verses.restored: On a Sabbath he was passing through grainfields, and his disciples were plucking and eating heads of grain, rubbing them in their hands.

familiar.text: And it came to pass on the second sabbath after the first, that he went through the corn fields; and his disciples plucked the ears of corn, and did eat, rubbing them in their hands.

modern.text: One Sabbath Jesus was passing through the grainfields, and His disciples began to pick the heads of grain, rub them in their hands, and eat them.

original.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ⸀σαββάτῳ διαπορεύεσθαι αὐτὸν ⸀διὰ σπορίμων, καὶ ἔτιλλον οἱ μαθηταὶ αὐτοῦ ⸂καὶ ἤσθιον τοὺς στάχυας⸃ ψώχοντες ταῖς χερσίν.

verses.restored: Some of the Pharisees said, Why are you doing what is not lawful on the Sabbath?

familiar.text: And certain of the Pharisees said unto them, Why do ye that which is not lawful to do on the sabbath days?

modern.text: But some of the Pharisees asked, “Why are you doing what is unlawful on the Sabbath?”

original.text: τινὲς δὲ τῶν Φαρισαίων ⸀εἶπαν· Τί ποιεῖτε ὃ οὐκ ⸀ἔξεστιν τοῖς σάββασιν;

verses.restored: Jesus answered them, Have you not read what David did when he was hungry, he and those with him,

familiar.text: And Jesus answering them said, Have ye not read so much as this, what David did, when himself was an hungred, and they which were with him;

modern.text: Jesus replied, “Have you not read what David did when he and his companions were hungry?

original.text: καὶ ἀποκριθεὶς πρὸς αὐτοὺς εἶπεν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Οὐδὲ τοῦτο ἀνέγνωτε ὃ ἐποίησεν Δαυὶδ ⸀ὁπότε ἐπείνασεν αὐτὸς καὶ οἱ μετʼ αὐτοῦ ⸀ὄντες;

verses.restored: how he entered the house of the Divine, took the bread of the Presence, ate, and gave to those with him, which is not lawful to eat except for the priests alone?

familiar.text: How he went into the house of God, and did take and eat the shewbread, and gave also to them that were with him; which it is not lawful to eat but for the priests alone?

modern.text: He entered the house of God, took the consecrated bread and gave it to his companions, and ate what is lawful only for the priests to eat.”

original.text: ⸀ὡς εἰσῆλθεν εἰς τὸν οἶκον τοῦ θεοῦ καὶ τοὺς ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως ⸀λαβὼν ἔφαγεν καὶ ⸀ἔδωκεν τοῖς μετʼ αὐτοῦ, οὓς οὐκ ἔξεστιν φαγεῖν εἰ μὴ μόνους τοὺς ἱερεῖς;

verses.restored: He said to them, The Son of Humanity is lord of the Sabbath.

familiar.text: And he said unto them, That the Son of man is Lord also of the sabbath.

modern.text: Then Jesus declared, “The Son of Man is Lord of the Sabbath.” Jesus Heals on the Sabbath (Matthew 12:9–14; Mark 3:1–6)

original.text: καὶ ἔλεγεν ⸀αὐτοῖς· Κύριός ἐστιν ⸂τοῦ σαββάτου ὁ υἱὸς τοῦ ἀνθρώπου⸃.

verses.restored: On another Sabbath, he entered the synagogue and taught. A man was there whose right hand was withered.

familiar.text: And it came to pass also on another sabbath, that he entered into the synagogue and taught: and there was a man whose right hand was withered.

modern.text: On another Sabbath Jesus entered the synagogue and was teaching, and a man was there whose right hand was withered.

original.text: Ἐγένετο ⸀δὲ ἐν ἑτέρῳ σαββάτῳ εἰσελθεῖν αὐτὸν εἰς τὴν συναγωγὴν καὶ διδάσκειν· καὶ ἦν ⸂ἄνθρωπος ἐκεῖ⸃ καὶ ἡ χεὶρ αὐτοῦ ἡ δεξιὰ ἦν ξηρά·

verses.restored: The scribes and Pharisees were watching him closely, whether he would heal on the Sabbath, so that they might find an accusation against him.

familiar.text: And the scribes and Pharisees watched him, whether he would heal on the sabbath day; that they might find an accusation against him.

modern.text: Looking for a reason to accuse Jesus, the scribes and Pharisees were watching Him closely to see if He would heal on the Sabbath.

original.text: ⸀παρετηροῦντο ⸀δὲ οἱ γραμματεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι εἰ ἐν τῷ σαββάτῳ ⸀θεραπεύει, ἵνα εὕρωσιν ⸀κατηγορεῖν αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: He knew their reasonings and said to the man with the withered hand, Rise and stand in the middle. He rose and stood.

familiar.text: But he knew their thoughts, and said to the man which had the withered hand, Rise up, and stand forth in the midst. And he arose and stood forth.

modern.text: But Jesus knew their thoughts and said to the man with the withered hand, “Get up and stand among us.” So he got up and stood there.

original.text: αὐτὸς δὲ ᾔδει τοὺς διαλογισμοὺς αὐτῶν, ⸂εἶπεν δὲ⸃ τῷ ⸀ἀνδρὶ τῷ ξηρὰν ἔχοντι τὴν χεῖρα· ⸀Ἔγειρε καὶ στῆθι εἰς τὸ μέσον· ⸀καὶ ἀναστὰς ἔστη.

verses.restored: Jesus said to them, I ask you: Is it lawful on the Sabbath to do good or to do harm, to save life/soul or to destroy?

familiar.text: Then said Jesus unto them, I will ask you one thing; Is it lawful on the sabbath days to do good, or to do evil? to save life, or to destroy it?

modern.text: Then Jesus said to them, “I ask you, which is lawful on the Sabbath: to do good or to do evil, to save life or to destroy it?”

original.text: εἶπεν ⸀δὲ ὁ Ἰησοῦς πρὸς αὐτούς· ⸀Ἐπερωτῶ ὑμᾶς, ⸀εἰ ἔξεστιν ⸂τῷ σαββάτῳ⸃ ἀγαθοποιῆσαι ἢ κακοποιῆσαι, ψυχὴν σῶσαι ἢ ⸀ἀπολέσαι;

verses.restored: Looking around at them all, he said to him, Stretch out your hand. He did, and his hand was restored.

familiar.text: And looking round about upon them all, he said unto the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he did so: and his hand was restored whole as the other.

modern.text: And after looking around at all of them, He said to the man, “Stretch out your hand.” He did so, and it was restored.

original.text: καὶ περιβλεψάμενος πάντας αὐτοὺς εἶπεν αὐτῷ· Ἔκτεινον τὴν χεῖρά σου· ὁ δὲ ἐποίησεν, καὶ ἀπεκατεστάθη ἡ χεὶρ ⸀αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: They were filled with mindless fury and discussed with one another what they might do to Jesus.

familiar.text: And they were filled with madness; and communed one with another what they might do to Jesus.

modern.text: But the scribes and Pharisees were filled with rage and began to discuss with one another what they might do to Jesus. The Twelve Apostles (Matthew 10:1–4; Mark 3:13–19)

original.text: αὐτοὶ δὲ ἐπλήσθησαν ἀνοίας, καὶ διελάλουν πρὸς ἀλλήλους τί ἂν ποιήσαιεν τῷ Ἰησοῦ.

verses.restored: In these days he went out to the mountain to pray, and he spent the night in prayer to the Divine.

familiar.text: And it came to pass in those days, that he went out into a mountain to pray, and continued all night in prayer to God.

modern.text: In those days Jesus went out to the mountain to pray, and He spent the night in prayer to God.

original.text: Ἐγένετο δὲ ἐν ταῖς ἡμέραις ταύταις ⸂ἐξελθεῖν αὐτὸν⸃ εἰς τὸ ὄρος προσεύξασθαι, καὶ ἦν διανυκτερεύων ἐν τῇ προσευχῇ τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: When day came, he called his disciples and chose from them twelve, whom he also named apostles/sent ones.

familiar.text: And when it was day, he called unto him his disciples: and of them he chose twelve, whom also he named apostles;

modern.text: When daylight came, He called His disciples to Him and chose twelve of them, whom He also designated as apostles:

original.text: καὶ ὅτε ἐγένετο ἡμέρα, προσεφώνησεν τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἐκλεξάμενος ἀπʼ αὐτῶν δώδεκα, οὓς καὶ ἀποστόλους ὠνόμασεν,

verses.restored: Simon, whom he also named Peter, Andrew his brother, James, John, Philip, Bartholomew,

familiar.text: Simon, (whom he also named Peter,) and Andrew his brother, James and John, Philip and Bartholomew,

modern.text: Simon, whom He named Peter, and his brother Andrew; James and John; Philip and Bartholomew;

original.text: Σίμωνα ὃν καὶ ὠνόμασεν Πέτρον καὶ Ἀνδρέαν τὸν ἀδελφὸν αὐτοῦ ⸀καὶ Ἰάκωβον καὶ Ἰωάννην ⸁καὶ Φίλιππον καὶ Βαρθολομαῖον

verses.restored: Matthew, Thomas, James son of Alphaeus, Simon called Zealot,

familiar.text: Matthew and Thomas, James the son of Alphaeus, and Simon called Zelotes,

modern.text: Matthew and Thomas; James son of Alphaeus and Simon called the Zealot;

original.text: ⸀καὶ Μαθθαῖον καὶ Θωμᾶν ⸁καὶ ⸀Ἰάκωβον Ἁλφαίου καὶ Σίμωνα τὸν καλούμενον Ζηλωτὴν

verses.restored: Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a betrayer.

familiar.text: And Judas the brother of James, and Judas Iscariot, which also was the traitor.

modern.text: Judas son of James, and Judas Iscariot, who became a traitor. Jesus Heals the Multitudes (Matthew 4:23–25; Mark 3:7–12)

original.text: ⸀καὶ Ἰούδαν Ἰακώβου καὶ Ἰούδαν ⸀Ἰσκαριὼθ ⸀ὃς ἐγένετο προδότης.

verses.restored: Coming down with them, he stood on a level place, with a great crowd of his disciples and a great multitude of people from all Judea, Jerusalem, and the coastal region of Tyre and Sidon.

familiar.text: And he came down with them, and stood in the plain, and the company of his disciples, and a great multitude of people out of all Judaea and Jerusalem, and from the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon, which came to hear him, and to be healed of their diseases;

modern.text: Then Jesus came down with them and stood on a level place. A large crowd of His disciples was there, along with a great number of people from all over Judea, Jerusalem, and the sea coast of Tyre and Sidon.

original.text: Καὶ καταβὰς μετʼ αὐτῶν ἔστη ἐπὶ τόπου πεδινοῦ, καὶ ὄχλος ⸀πολὺς μαθητῶν αὐτοῦ, καὶ πλῆθος πολὺ τοῦ λαοῦ ἀπὸ πάσης τῆς Ἰουδαίας καὶ Ἰερουσαλὴμ καὶ τῆς παραλίου Τύρου καὶ Σιδῶνος,

verses.restored: They came to hear him and to be healed from their diseases; those troubled by unclean spirits were healed.

familiar.text: And they that were vexed with unclean spirits: and they were healed.

modern.text: They had come to hear Him and to be healed of their diseases, and those troubled by unclean spirits were healed.

original.text: οἳ ἦλθον ἀκοῦσαι αὐτοῦ καὶ ἰαθῆναι ἀπὸ τῶν νόσων αὐτῶν· καὶ οἱ ⸂ἐνοχλούμενοι ἀπὸ⸃ πνευμάτων ⸀ἀκαθάρτων ἐθεραπεύοντο·

verses.restored: All the crowd sought to touch him, because power was going out from him and healing all.

familiar.text: And the whole multitude sought to touch him: for there went virtue out of him, and healed them all.

modern.text: The entire crowd was trying to touch Him, because power was coming from Him and healing them all. The Beatitudes (Psalms 1:1–6; Matthew 5:3–12)

original.text: καὶ πᾶς ὁ ὄχλος ⸀ἐζήτουν ἅπτεσθαι αὐτοῦ, ὅτι δύναμις παρʼ αὐτοῦ ἐξήρχετο καὶ ἰᾶτο πάντας.

verses.restored: Lifting up his eyes to his disciples, he said: Blessed/flourishing are you poor, because yours is the reign of the Divine.

familiar.text: And he lifted up his eyes on his disciples, and said, Blessed be ye poor: for yours is the kingdom of God.

modern.text: Looking up at His disciples, Jesus said: “Blessed are you who are poor, for yours is the kingdom of God.

original.text: Καὶ αὐτὸς ἐπάρας τοὺς ὀφθαλμοὺς αὐτοῦ εἰς τοὺς μαθητὰς αὐτοῦ ἔλεγεν· Μακάριοι οἱ πτωχοί, ὅτι ὑμετέρα ἐστὶν ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ.

verses.restored: Blessed/flourishing are you who hunger now, because you will be filled. Blessed/flourishing are you who weep now, because you will laugh.

familiar.text: Blessed are ye that hunger now: for ye shall be filled. Blessed are ye that weep now: for ye shall laugh.

modern.text: Blessed are you who hunger now, for you will be filled. Blessed are you who weep now, for you will laugh.

original.text: μακάριοι οἱ πεινῶντες νῦν, ὅτι χορτασθήσεσθε. μακάριοι οἱ κλαίοντες νῦν, ὅτι γελάσετε.

verses.restored: Blessed/flourishing are you when people hate you, exclude you, insult you, and reject your name as harmful because of the Son of Humanity.

familiar.text: Blessed are ye, when men shall hate you, and when they shall separate you from their company, and shall reproach you, and cast out your name as evil, for the Son of man’s sake.

modern.text: Blessed are you when people hate you, and when they exclude you and insult you and reject your name as evil because of the Son of Man.

original.text: Μακάριοί ἐστε ὅταν μισήσωσιν ὑμᾶς οἱ ἄνθρωποι, καὶ ὅταν ἀφορίσωσιν ὑμᾶς καὶ ὀνειδίσωσιν καὶ ἐκβάλωσιν τὸ ὄνομα ὑμῶν ὡς πονηρὸν ἕνεκα τοῦ υἱοῦ τοῦ ἀνθρώπου·

verses.restored: Rejoice in that day and leap, for look, your reward is great in heaven; for their fathers did likewise to the prophets.

familiar.text: Rejoice ye in that day, and leap for joy: for, behold, your reward is great in heaven: for in the like manner did their fathers unto the prophets.

modern.text: Rejoice in that day and leap for joy, because great is your reward in heaven. For their fathers treated the prophets in the same way. Woes to the Satisfied (Amos 6:1–7)

original.text: χάρητε ἐν ἐκείνῃ τῇ ἡμέρᾳ καὶ σκιρτήσατε, ἰδοὺ γὰρ ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολὺς ἐν τῷ οὐρανῷ· κατὰ ⸂τὰ αὐτὰ⸃ γὰρ ἐποίουν τοῖς προφήταις οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: But woe to you rich, because you have received your consolation.

familiar.text: But woe unto you that are rich! for ye have received your consolation.

modern.text: But woe to you who are rich, for you have already received your comfort.

original.text: πλὴν οὐαὶ ὑμῖν τοῖς πλουσίοις, ὅτι ἀπέχετε τὴν παράκλησιν ὑμῶν.

verses.restored: Woe to you who are full now, because you will hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, because you will mourn and weep.

familiar.text: Woe unto you that are full! for ye shall hunger. Woe unto you that laugh now! for ye shall mourn and weep.

modern.text: Woe to you who are well fed now, for you will hunger. Woe to you who laugh now, for you will mourn and weep.

original.text: οὐαὶ ὑμῖν, οἱ ἐμπεπλησμένοι ⸀νῦν, ὅτι πεινάσετε. ⸀οὐαί, οἱ γελῶντες νῦν, ὅτι πενθήσετε καὶ κλαύσετε.

verses.restored: Woe when all people speak beautifully of you, for their fathers did likewise to the false prophets.

familiar.text: Woe unto you, when all men shall speak well of you! for so did their fathers to the false prophets.

modern.text: Woe to you when all men speak well of you, for their fathers treated the false prophets in the same way. Love Your Enemies (Matthew 5:38–48)

original.text: Οὐαὶ ὅταν ⸂καλῶς ὑμᾶς⸃ εἴπωσιν ⸀πάντες οἱ ἄνθρωποι, κατὰ ⸂τὰ αὐτὰ⸃ γὰρ ἐποίουν τοῖς ψευδοπροφήταις οἱ πατέρες αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: But to you who hear I say: love your enemies, do beautiful/good to those who hate you,

familiar.text: But I say unto you which hear, Love your enemies, do good to them which hate you,

modern.text: But to those of you who will listen, I say: Love your enemies, do good to those who hate you,

original.text: Ἀλλὰ ὑμῖν λέγω τοῖς ἀκούουσιν, ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν, καλῶς ποιεῖτε τοῖς μισοῦσιν ὑμᾶς,

verses.restored: bless those who curse you, pray concerning those who mistreat you.

familiar.text: Bless them that curse you, and pray for them which despitefully use you.

modern.text: bless those who curse you, pray for those who mistreat you.

original.text: εὐλογεῖτε τοὺς καταρωμένους ⸀ὑμᾶς, προσεύχεσθε ⸀περὶ τῶν ἐπηρεαζόντων ὑμᾶς.

verses.restored: To the one striking you on the cheek, offer also the other; from the one taking your cloak, do not withhold the tunic also.

familiar.text: And unto him that smiteth thee on the one cheek offer also the other; and him that taketh away thy cloak forbid not to take thy coat also.

modern.text: If someone strikes you on one cheek, turn to him the other also. And if someone takes your cloak, do not withhold your tunic as well.

original.text: τῷ τύπτοντί σε ἐπὶ τὴν σιαγόνα πάρεχε καὶ τὴν ἄλλην, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντός σου τὸ ἱμάτιον καὶ τὸν χιτῶνα μὴ κωλύσῃς.

verses.restored: Give to everyone asking you, and from the one taking what is yours, do not demand it back.

familiar.text: Give to every man that asketh of thee; and of him that taketh away thy goods ask them not again.

modern.text: Give to everyone who asks you, and if anyone takes what is yours, do not demand it back.

original.text: ⸀παντὶ αἰτοῦντί σε δίδου, καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ αἴροντος τὰ σὰ μὴ ἀπαίτει.

verses.restored: Just as you want people to do to you, do likewise to them.

familiar.text: And as ye would that men should do to you, do ye also to them likewise.

modern.text: Do to others as you would have them do to you.

original.text: καὶ καθὼς θέλετε ἵνα ποιῶσιν ὑμῖν οἱ ⸀ἄνθρωποι, ποιεῖτε αὐτοῖς ὁμοίως.

verses.restored: If you love those loving you, what grace is that to you? For even sinners/misaligned ones love those loving them.

familiar.text: For if ye love them which love you, what thank have ye? for sinners also love those that love them.

modern.text: If you love those who love you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners love those who love them.

original.text: Καὶ εἰ ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας ὑμᾶς, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν; καὶ γὰρ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ τοὺς ἀγαπῶντας αὐτοὺς ἀγαπῶσιν.

verses.restored: If you do good to those doing good to you, what grace is that to you? Even sinners/misaligned ones do the same.

familiar.text: And if ye do good to them which do good to you, what thank have ye? for sinners also do even the same.

modern.text: If you do good to those who do good to you, what credit is that to you? Even sinners do the same.

original.text: ⸀καὶ ἐὰν ἀγαθοποιῆτε τοὺς ἀγαθοποιοῦντας ὑμᾶς, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν; ⸁καὶ οἱ ἁμαρτωλοὶ τὸ αὐτὸ ποιοῦσιν.

verses.restored: If you lend to those from whom you hope to receive, what grace is that to you? Even sinners/misaligned ones lend to sinners/misaligned ones to receive back the same.

familiar.text: And if ye lend to them of whom ye hope to receive, what thank have ye? for sinners also lend to sinners, to receive as much again.

modern.text: And if you lend to those from whom you expect repayment, what credit is that to you? Even sinners lend to sinners, expecting to be repaid in full.

original.text: καὶ ἐὰν ⸀δανίσητε παρʼ ὧν ἐλπίζετε ⸀λαβεῖν, ποία ὑμῖν χάρις ἐστίν; ⸀καὶ ἁμαρτωλοὶ ἁμαρτωλοῖς δανίζουσιν ἵνα ἀπολάβωσιν τὰ ἴσα.

verses.restored: But love your enemies, do good, and lend, expecting nothing back; your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High, because he is kind to the ungrateful and harmful.

familiar.text: But love ye your enemies, and do good, and lend, hoping for nothing again; and your reward shall be great, and ye shall be the children of the Highest: for he is kind unto the unthankful and to the evil.

modern.text: But love your enemies, do good to them, and lend to them, expecting nothing in return. Then your reward will be great, and you will be sons of the Most High; for He is kind to the ungrateful and wicked.

original.text: πλὴν ἀγαπᾶτε τοὺς ἐχθροὺς ὑμῶν καὶ ἀγαθοποιεῖτε καὶ δανίζετε μηδὲν ἀπελπίζοντες· καὶ ἔσται ὁ μισθὸς ὑμῶν πολύς, καὶ ἔσεσθε υἱοὶ Ὑψίστου, ὅτι αὐτὸς χρηστός ἐστιν ἐπὶ τοὺς ἀχαρίστους καὶ πονηρούς.

verses.restored: Become merciful, just as your Father is merciful.

familiar.text: Be ye therefore merciful, as your Father also is merciful.

modern.text: Be merciful, just as your Father is merciful. Judging Others (Matthew 7:1–6; Romans 14:1–12)

original.text: ⸀γίνεσθε οἰκτίρμονες ⸀καθὼς ὁ πατὴρ ὑμῶν οἰκτίρμων ἐστίν·

verses.restored: Do not judge, and you will certainly not be judged; do not condemn, and you will certainly not be condemned; release, and you will be released.

familiar.text: Judge not, and ye shall not be judged: condemn not, and ye shall not be condemned: forgive, and ye shall be forgiven:

modern.text: Do not judge, and you will not be judged. Do not condemn, and you will not be condemned. Forgive, and you will be forgiven.

original.text: Καὶ μὴ κρίνετε, καὶ οὐ μὴ κριθῆτε· ⸀καὶ μὴ καταδικάζετε, καὶ οὐ μὴ καταδικασθῆτε. ἀπολύετε, καὶ ἀπολυθήσεσθε·

verses.restored: Give, and it will be given to you: good measure, pressed down, shaken together, running over, they will give into your lap; for with the measure you measure, it will be measured back to you.

familiar.text: Give, and it shall be given unto you; good measure, pressed down, and shaken together, and running over, shall men give into your bosom. For with the same measure that ye mete withal it shall be measured to you again.

modern.text: Give, and it will be given to you. A good measure, pressed down, shaken together, and running over will be poured into your lap. For with the measure you use, it will be measured back to you.”

original.text: δίδοτε, καὶ δοθήσεται ὑμῖν· μέτρον καλὸν πεπιεσμένον ⸀σεσαλευμένον ὑπερεκχυννόμενον δώσουσιν εἰς τὸν κόλπον ὑμῶν· ⸂ᾧ γὰρ μέτρῳ⸃ μετρεῖτε ἀντιμετρηθήσεται ὑμῖν.

verses.restored: He also spoke a parable to them: Can a blind person guide a blind person? Will not both fall into a pit?

familiar.text: And he spake a parable unto them, Can the blind lead the blind? shall they not both fall into the ditch?

modern.text: Jesus also told them a parable: “Can a blind man lead a blind man? Will they not both fall into a pit?

original.text: Εἶπεν δὲ ⸀καὶ παραβολὴν αὐτοῖς· Μήτι δύναται τυφλὸς τυφλὸν ὁδηγεῖν; οὐχὶ ἀμφότεροι εἰς βόθυνον ⸀ἐμπεσοῦνται;

verses.restored: A disciple is not above the teacher, but everyone fully formed will be like the teacher.

familiar.text: The disciple is not above his master: but every one that is perfect shall be as his master.

modern.text: A disciple is not above his teacher, but everyone who is fully trained will be like his teacher.

original.text: οὐκ ἔστιν μαθητὴς ὑπὲρ τὸν ⸀διδάσκαλον, κατηρτισμένος δὲ πᾶς ἔσται ὡς ὁ διδάσκαλος αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Why do you look at the speck in your brother's eye, but do not notice the beam in your own eye?

familiar.text: And why beholdest thou the mote that is in thy brother’s eye, but perceivest not the beam that is in thine own eye?

modern.text: Why do you look at the speck in your brother’s eye, but fail to notice the beam in your own eye?

original.text: τί δὲ βλέπεις τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου, τὴν δὲ δοκὸν τὴν ἐν τῷ ἰδίῳ ὀφθαλμῷ οὐ κατανοεῖς;

verses.restored: How are you able to say to your brother, Brother, let me take out the speck in your eye, while you yourself do not see the beam in your eye? Hypocrite, first take the beam out of your eye, and then you will see clearly to take out the speck in your brother's eye.

familiar.text: Either how canst thou say to thy brother, Brother, let me pull out the mote that is in thine eye, when thou thyself beholdest not the beam that is in thine own eye? Thou hypocrite, cast out first the beam out of thine own eye, and then shalt thou see clearly to pull out the mote that is in thy brother’s eye.

modern.text: How can you say, ‘Brother, let me take the speck out of your eye,’ while you yourself fail to see the beam in your own eye? You hypocrite! First take the beam out of your own eye, and then you will see clearly to remove the speck from your brother’s eye. A Tree and Its Fruit (Matthew 7:15–23; Matthew 12:33–37)

original.text: ⸀πῶς δύνασαι λέγειν τῷ ἀδελφῷ σου· Ἀδελφέ, ἄφες ἐκβάλω τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σου, αὐτὸς τὴν ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ σοῦ δοκὸν οὐ βλέπων; ὑποκριτά, ἔκβαλε πρῶτον τὴν δοκὸν ἐκ τοῦ ὀφθαλμοῦ σοῦ, καὶ τότε διαβλέψεις ⸂τὸ κάρφος τὸ ἐν τῷ ὀφθαλμῷ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου ἐκβαλεῖν⸃.

verses.restored: For there is no beautiful/good tree making rotten fruit, nor again a rotten tree making beautiful/good fruit.

familiar.text: For a good tree bringeth not forth corrupt fruit; neither doth a corrupt tree bring forth good fruit.

modern.text: No good tree bears bad fruit, nor does a bad tree bear good fruit.

original.text: Οὐ γάρ ἐστιν δένδρον καλὸν ποιοῦν καρπὸν σαπρόν, οὐδὲ ⸀πάλιν δένδρον σαπρὸν ποιοῦν καρπὸν καλόν.

verses.restored: Each tree is known from its own fruit; for people do not gather figs from thorns, nor do they harvest grapes from a bramble bush.

familiar.text: For every tree is known by his own fruit. For of thorns men do not gather figs, nor of a bramble bush gather they grapes.

modern.text: For each tree is known by its own fruit. Indeed, figs are not gathered from thornbushes, nor grapes from brambles.

original.text: ἕκαστον γὰρ δένδρον ἐκ τοῦ ἰδίου καρποῦ γινώσκεται· οὐ γὰρ ἐξ ἀκανθῶν συλλέγουσιν σῦκα, οὐδὲ ἐκ βάτου ⸂σταφυλὴν τρυγῶσιν⸃.

verses.restored: The good person from the good treasure of the heart brings out good, and the harmful person from harmful treasure brings out harm; for from the abundance of the heart the mouth speaks.

familiar.text: A good man out of the good treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is good; and an evil man out of the evil treasure of his heart bringeth forth that which is evil: for of the abundance of the heart his mouth speaketh.

modern.text: The good man brings good things out of the good treasure of his heart, and the evil man brings evil things out of the evil treasure of his heart. For out of the overflow of the heart, the mouth speaks. The House on the Rock (Matthew 7:24–27)

original.text: ὁ ἀγαθὸς ἄνθρωπος ἐκ τοῦ ἀγαθοῦ θησαυροῦ τῆς καρδίας ⸀αὐτοῦ προφέρει τὸ ἀγαθόν, καὶ ὁ ⸀πονηρὸς ἐκ τοῦ ⸀πονηροῦ προφέρει τὸ πονηρόν· ἐκ γὰρ ⸀περισσεύματος καρδίας λαλεῖ τὸ στόμα αὐτοῦ.

verses.restored: Why do you call me Lord, Lord, and not do what I say?

familiar.text: And why call ye me, Lord, Lord, and do not the things which I say?

modern.text: Why do you call Me ‘Lord, Lord,’ but not do what I say?

original.text: Τί δέ με καλεῖτε· Κύριε κύριε, καὶ οὐ ποιεῖτε ἃ λέγω;

verses.restored: Everyone coming to me, hearing my words, and doing them, I will show you whom that one is like.

familiar.text: Whosoever cometh to me, and heareth my sayings, and doeth them, I will shew you to whom he is like:

modern.text: I will show you what he is like who comes to Me and hears My words and acts on them:

original.text: πᾶς ὁ ἐρχόμενος πρός με καὶ ἀκούων μου τῶν λόγων καὶ ποιῶν αὐτούς, ὑποδείξω ὑμῖν τίνι ἐστὶν ὅμοιος·

verses.restored: That one is like a person building a house, who dug deep and set foundation on rock. Flood came, the river broke against that house and was not strong enough to shake it, because it had been well built.

familiar.text: He is like a man which built an house, and digged deep, and laid the foundation on a rock: and when the flood arose, the stream beat vehemently upon that house, and could not shake it: for it was founded upon a rock.

modern.text: He is like a man building a house, who dug down deep and laid his foundation on the rock. When the flood came, the torrent crashed against that house but could not shake it, because it was well built.

original.text: ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομοῦντι οἰκίαν ὃς ἔσκαψεν καὶ ἐβάθυνεν καὶ ἔθηκεν θεμέλιον ἐπὶ τὴν πέτραν· πλημμύρης δὲ γενομένης προσέρηξεν ὁ ποταμὸς τῇ οἰκίᾳ ἐκείνῃ, καὶ οὐκ ἴσχυσεν σαλεῦσαι αὐτὴν ⸂διὰ τὸ καλῶς οἰκοδομῆσθαι αὐτήν⸃.

verses.restored: The one hearing and not doing is like a person building a house on the earth without foundation; the river broke against it, and immediately it fell, and the ruin of that house was great.

familiar.text: But he that heareth, and doeth not, is like a man that without a foundation built an house upon the earth; against which the stream did beat vehemently, and immediately it fell; and the ruin of that house was great.

modern.text: But the one who hears My words and does not act on them is like a man who built his house on ground without a foundation. The torrent crashed against that house, and immediately it fell—and great was its destruction!”

original.text: ὁ δὲ ἀκούσας καὶ μὴ ποιήσας ὅμοιός ἐστιν ἀνθρώπῳ οἰκοδομήσαντι οἰκίαν ἐπὶ τὴν γῆν χωρὶς θεμελίου, ᾗ προσέρηξεν ὁ ποταμός, καὶ ⸂εὐθὺς συνέπεσεν⸃, καὶ ἐγένετο τὸ ῥῆγμα τῆς οἰκίας ἐκείνης μέγα.
